Question: What's the best surprise you've ever received from your partner/lover?
Answer: It was my birthday on August 4th—my first birthday with him. Birthdays are special to me, and while I don’t go all out with extravagant celebrations, I do like to make the day count. So, a day before my birthday, my mister casually mentioned, "You know I don't celebrate birthdays, right? I don’t celebrate mine either, and I haven't got you anything. But we'll go for dinner, of course." I tried to play it cool and responded, "It’s fine, I don’t mind" ( of course, I did—though not because of the gift). Then he added, "I hope you don't believe in 12 AM wishes?" I said, "No, not at all." (Totally rolling my eyes now) I made up my mind that he wouldn’t wish me at midnight, so when the clock struck 12…. He sent a beautiful text that left me overjoyed. Who does that after making it seem like he wouldn’t? (Deep down, I knew he would, ahem). The next day, we met up, and he brought along a cool, aesthetic, and delicious cake. Also, did I mention he was twinning with me 👀 After we cut the cake, he suddenly turned to me and said, "Please close your eyes." I was clueless, standing there with my eyes shut, while "Love Story" by Taylor Swift played in the background. Still, I didn’t suspect anything. Then I heard him say, "Show me your hand," and the next thing I knew, he was sliding a ring onto my finger. How cool is that? I was speechless, completely caught off guard, and absolutely on cloud nine. I felt so special. So, as the question asks—what’s the best surprise from your partner? This was the best so far. And I know, My Mister, you’re reading this—I’m looking forward to many more amazing surprises for a lifetime, haha! Rabiya PS - No evil eyes please, Lol. Say Masha allah please.

Question: What did you do today?
Answer: As I stepped into the hallowed halls of the courthouse that morning, I couldn't help but feel a mix of excitement and nerves. It was my first time here, and I wanted to make a good impression. Dressed in my crisp, professional uniform, I was determined to show respect for the solemnity of the place. Little did I know that the day had a hilarious surprise in store for me. The rhythm of the court was in full swing, and it seemed like everyone knew exactly what they were doing. Everyone, that is, except me. You see, every case in that courtroom had not just a case number but also a special serial number assigned for reference. And as fate would have it, that was the part I had overlooked in my preparations. Undeterred, I confidently stepped before the judge and began stating my case number with utmost clarity. The judge listened attentively, but to my surprise, she interrupted me and inquired, "What is the serial number?" My heart sank, and my mind went blank. It felt like an eternity as I stood there, flustered and unsure of what to say. It was as if all the courtroom etiquette I had practised had vanished into thin air. Luckily, the court clerk came to my rescue. With a knowing smile, he whispered the right serial number. Throughout the rest of the proceedings, my initial awkwardness began to fade, replaced by a newfound sense of confidence and humility. I learned that everyone, even in a serious setting like a courtroom, is prone to making mistakes, and that's alright. It's all part of the learning process. As the day progressed, I observed the intricacies of the legal system, marvelled at the eloquence of the attorneys, and empathised with the individuals entangled in various legal battles. From the tense moments to the occasional lighthearted exchanges between lawyers, it was a rollercoaster of emotions. So, as I reflect on that day, I can't help but smile at my courtroom adventure. It's a story I'll cherish for a lifetime and one that reminds me that even in serious situations, laughter and the ability to laugh at oneself can lighten the heaviest of hearts. Here's to more learning experiences and unexpected moments of humour on our life journeys! PS - In case we are meeting for the first time, I am a business and corporate lawyer. Connect with me if you think, I can help you with your legal issues. All the relevant links are in my bio. Rabiya

Question: What motivates you to study and why?
Answer: I wasn't studying since four days because I had to complete my court internship diary and submit it in the university. I was busy doing that. I was lying on my bed, awake. All I can do is cry and weep for a while and get back to work. I knew I just want to beat this initial resistance and then I would be fine. I knew that once I reach my study table, I would not get up before completing atleast one chapter. Lost in the past. Lost in the people who left. Lost in the people who are to come. I study late till night many atimes. Whenever I don't know what to do in life. When the fear of failure hits me hard that I end up crying my soul out, when the uncertain future to come, scares me to hell, I just go and stand outside my parents room. I just see them. I sit near the door and hear them snoring (haha). It makes me cry. It makes me feel something. It breaks me but also at the same time rebuilds me. I just look at them and get back to studying. Because that's the only way, I can do something from them. I can try to pay back to them. My parents and their dream to see me succeed is enough to beat that initial resistance and start getting some shit done. If not for myself, I do it for them. And that's enough to get me going and I hope it gets you going too. All the best ! Rabiya

Question: What are you going through in life right now?
Answer: We all learnt about punctuation marks in school. A comma or semicolon causes you to take a little break from reading. A full stop is where you allow yourself to breath before you move ahead. An exclamation mark is used to put an extra emphasis. But there is this another, lesser known punctuation mark. You know which one is it ? Let me give you hints - It doesn't merely cause you to take a breath. It doesn't lead you to the next paragraph. Rather, It forces you to put the book down, altogether. Shut completely. The harshest of all punctuation marks. Grief. There is no moving to the following sentence. It basically reads ‘Stop’ in the middle of everything. And you do. And suddenly there is nothing. The part where you analyze the grief and live in its void. That part is difficult. So, so difficult. But.. After you have soaked all the grief in, There comes a time where courage flushes your cheeks and you pick up the book again. There's something. Something new. It's full of promising words and curiosity that makes you giggle. It tells the tales of adventure and discovery. Several pages are still blank. And you know the good news ? You can write, whatever you wish for. Joy, reinstalled. Hope takes flight. And I must say, this joy is sweeter than before. It buzzes inside your chest and makes you laugh all the time. You feel like crying out of gratitude. Because you lived in the state of numbness for too long. You fought battles every day with yourself. You crafted this prayer. Indeed with hardship comes ease. After the rain, sun comes out. Every single time, without fail. Rabiya

I am infact running 2 weeks behind my planned schedule. While things are not in my favor today, I know for a matter of fact that they will be in future. I will have to do that for myself. I just panic and then figure it out on my own. May be this post is just about it. I know I will make it. It's just matter of 70–80 days now. I am ready to put whatever it takes. I am writing this, so that I can come to this post few years later. Things would have been changed by then, Perhaps. Challenges would be bigger than today but what will remain constant is - my self doubt, my panic and after all the panic, getting things done. This is reminder for my future self - You haven't come this far, just to come this far. You made it till here, so believe that you will make it ahead too. Rabiya

Question: What’s your purpose of helping others?
Answer: “It's your final exam. The sole basis of your graduation and one of your classmate forgot to bring essentials for exam. If you help him, he will be a tough competition to you and thereby, you will risk your position. With that being said, how many of you will help your classmate?” - Asked our HR professor. And when I see this things happening - from a distance, it gives me a satisfactory feeling. It makes me happy. I sleep with a light heart. Question: Can you feel someone's love for you?
Answer: I stay busy most of the days. Managing two professional courses simultaneously is a task and well it takes a lot to keep up with both of them. My days just goes around studying stuff. My university exams ended last week and I will be entering 5th and the last year of my graduation (Bcom LLB Hons.). Ahh, time flies and thanks to Covid, I lost 2 years of my college life to it. After exams got over and I didn't take a break, not even for a day and started making up with classes of CA Intermediate and I have been busy since then. Look around, love is present everywhere in tiny bits and you ignore it all the time. P.S- Hey,future husband I can baby sit kids as well..XD Rabiya

Question: What should I do for being different?
Answer: I have been a person who always wanted approval, attention and appreciation. I made every effort to get it. No matter what I did, I fairly got any of these. I wanted to be a popular among my seniors and teachers at school. I studied well, managed to get a rank, performed on the stage but still it didn't do any wonders to me. No matter what, I wanted attention. I did crazy things. None of which helped me get it. On the other hand, there were friends of mine, who fairly did anything and still got all that attention. I used to dispise them. Now, when I look back, I realize that I spent so many years of my life seeking validation, wanting attention from the other people. For what ? Just so that people would recognize me or would talk about me but does that really matter ? Today, at my college - all my professors know me, all my classmates know me, few of my seniors know me and I am unknown among my juniors. All of these, does it matter today ? Not really. My professors know me today because I have proved that I am worthy to be known. My classmates cherish for me because I have helped them. My seniors know me because I have worked with them. My juniors don't know me because I never went to freshers party. Today I am not desperate to gain attention of the people. Today I get attention because of the way I am. The way I work, the way I represent myself. I don't do the talking, my actions speaks for myself. Attention is just the by product that comes with it. Let people like you the way you are - as flawed as you might me, as unattractive as you are or as unaccomplished as you are. If you want to be different, be different because you want it and not because you want others to see your difference. If you want to be different, be different in your own skin. Make your strengths so strong that it makes you outshine among the rest. Rabiya

Question: Be honest, why do you write on Quora?
Answer: I was born with a average look, average personality, average know-abouts of the world. I never had that extraordinary skill which made me a popular high school student. Never had that pretty face which got me laid nor did I had great communication skills to outshine others. I remained averagely popular student whose identity was confined to her classmates, teachers who saw some sort of potential and few little kids of the school with whom I have small yet very intriguing memories. I always knew I was more than someone who managed to get into top 10 of students. I always wanted people to know that I am something more than a typical geek or nerd personality. Guess what, I failed badly in prove this. What can you even expect from a fat and ugly looking girl who had zero self-esteem of her own. Everytime I think about my past self, each time I brush up childhood memories it delivers a kick to some part of my mind and kind of brings a very brief moment of regret or grief whatever you call it. On the other hand, I believe if I try to erase my past self,I will destroy my present self because the past has mould me into something worthfull,atleast that is what I would like to believe. It's been a year I started writing here on Quora, never in my dreams I would have contemplated this. Few things have changed - I lost some weight, I look less ugly than before, my round chubby face looks oblong now (maybe), I am more confident except for the fact that I still haven't got laid,haha and I don't even want to get laid. Quora has given me a sort of assurance that in the loud noises of this world, my tiny voice still can be heard. I am a close knit person in reality and I can't digest the fact someone getting close to me, it just scares me to hell but I don't know how effortlessly I sometimes share tiny details of my life here on the internet where it is accessible to all. I never had that attention part going around me but here when I recieve messages from people, it makes go crazy that people remember things I wrote months back. The way they interpret my bio, the way some people always fascinate about whether some incident is real or just fiction ? Some guyz want to get married to me ( I will cry on my wedding because someone actually agreed to marry me), few school going kids seek inspiration from me, some are sailing in the same boat as mine and seeing all these love and praise coming towards it gives me an unknown sort of comfort. It gives me a feeling that I can be loveable, I can change people's perception by my words, I can write relatable things. No matter for how long I write here or before I get lost some other way around, I know that a part of me will always remain here and it in itself is a solace. To all the readers - Thank you for reading all my blabbering. I am always and always grateful to you guyz.

Question: What do you like to do when you are feeling low?
Answer: I plan. I set higher targets for myself. We tend to feel low when things don't go our way. Failures and disappointments are part of life and there should be a way to deal with it. One need break and recreation time to remain but I know when I deserve that break and when I don't. I can't chill watching a movie when I know I haven't completed my targets for the week. See, I can watch a movie, go for an outing, do an episode of emotional eating. There are innumerable ways, but I believe this will distract me for a while but at the of the day, I will have to face the reality and deal with it. There can be any sort of reason for me feeling low. Personal, emotional, academical or whatever. These failures and disappointment ignites something inside and I become more goal oriented. I find my motivation in my failures. I find motivation in rejections. I find motivation in humiliation. I find motivation in disappointments. I find motivation in awkwardness. I find motivation in silence. Negatives get inside me and push me to work harder than before. Constant self doubt and fear of failure keeps me going. Your past situation should never be a deciding factor for your tomorrow. Constantly work on changing your present, so that your tomorrow can be better. If you get comfortable in your present circumstances you will never be able to grow. There is always something inside me that wants change in my current situation and because I want that change, I consciously work for it. Rabiya

Question: What are some things most people take for granted?
Answer: Guess, who is studying on Sunday ?? I always mention to my friends, when they ask me about my weekends? “Jab zindagi jhandwa, toh phir kya sundwa, kya mondwa” - typical reply, you know. At some point of time, they would have also dreamed about getting into Inter. Studying new subjects, attending lectures and working hard double the amount but sadly they couldn't make it. Getting to work hard. Taking that pressure. Squeezing your brain hard to get the concepts and Studying until your back hurts - this are few things that people do crave for. People who couldn't make it through crave for this. While I study, I always make sure that I do it because I wanted to do it and when I am getting to do it, I should not complain and whine about it. We never enjoy where we are. We always want to get better and that's great but what about today ? Yesterday, all you wanted was today and now when you have today, just look at you, you are so lost in tomorrow. Rabiya

Question: How did you avoid your distractions while studying?
Answer: You get distracted because you can afford getting distracted. You get distracted because you have the time to get distracted. You get distracted because you don't value your time and efforts. Isn't it true that whenever you get distracted or start wasting your time, you subconsciously know that you are supposed to do something productive, something useful. How many of us listen to our subconscious ? We keep getting distracted and one day we realize that it's too late for not being distracted. The precious time you had in which you could have done something for your future self is gone far long. The biggest distraction we all currently have right now is Mobile phone. Everyone knows this and agrees to this. But tell me how many of us actually try to get away from this distraction. We keep phone just besides our books while studying. We keep checking notifications. We knowingly waste time in the name of study. Have you ever tried keeping your phone away from your study space ? Have you ever tried giving up that urge to not check the notifications every hour ? The truth is very few of us are able to do this and majority of us get tangled in this distractions and then regret it later. I will tell you my thing. I am not a saint either. One weekends my phone screen time is more than 7hours but on weekdays when I know I can't afford getting distracted my screen time is around 45–50mins. Yes, that's how I do it. I keep my phone away. In the cupboard far from my study space. I have figured out my biggest distraction and I stay away from it. Simple. I always say - Just know your WHY. Why you want to not get distracted ? Why you want to be productive and get things done ? You already have your answers. Keep that in mind. Keep your WHY's in your mind and you will overcome every - ‘How to’. If you don't separate your goals from your distractions then one day your distractions will separate you from your goal. Rabiya

Question: Can you share your 40 days study plan for your entrance exams?
Answer: I have received many requests to share my routine as to how I managed to study 13– 14hours and cracked the entrance exam. My routine some what looked like this - This was daily schedule. I have never been night owl earlier but one day I pulled an all nighter and messed up my daily routine, so I had to stick on the night study plan. I found it very peaceful to study at night because there were no disturbances around. Studying for such long hours that too continuously for many days can make you feel burned out but for me the incomplete syllabus always gave me that kick to study no matter what. I believe in the presence of god very heartfully and I usually planned my day around prayers , so that I don't miss any of them. Prayer is like a meditation and god is like a friend to me. Sometimes I used to cry sitting on the prayer mat because I used to feel very frustrated and helpless. Crying has always been therapeutic for me and it somehow gave me strength to push myself further. Having conversation with god made me feel calm and composed. It gave me a feeling that things are doable. Make sure you have a venting out system because you may need it. Be it God himself, a friend, a diary or whatever. Take all the stress out from your mind. There were times when I felt like giving up. There were time where things seemed very impossible to me but then they say - what doesn't kill you, makes you strong. I also got food poisoning and it wasted my three precious days and it disrupted my study plan but I picked myself up and kept going. Incorporate a fun element for yourself if possible. I daily used to watch one episode of my favorite show doubling the playback speed. I somehow managed to fit that in my schedule at the end of my big study session. You can personally tweak the schedule ofcourse according to your needs and routine. One advice - If you have plenty of time, take proper sleep and don't leave things for last minute. Don't procrastinate. Use your time wisely and take care of your physical and mental health. Just know your “WHY" and finding your “HOW” will not be too difficult. Wishing you all the good luck. Rabiya

Question: Why do we fall out of love?
Answer: You like a guy. You text him. He texts back. You write blogs. He make videos. Due to the high digital presence you get to know one another through each other's respective works. He asks for your phone number. You give. He sends you every picture of yours that you posted on your blog. He gave you a cute name. It makes you feel aww and special. You kind of start flirting with one another. It seems like it is mutual from both the side but it's still getting to know each other stage. He has exams. You wish him everyday. You have presentations. He wishes you everyday. Days pass. You talk. Feels like you found him. He is the one. The one you have been waiting for. He proposes you.You marry him. Go to honeymoon. Have kids. Ofcourse in your imagination. In real, you are not a couple yet but you know somewhere something something is there. Again days pass. You take it forward. One day he doesn't text you for the whole day. You wait and wait. You finally text him at night. It was last. You both never talked to one another after that. You feel like it was your mistake. You want to unsend every text you sent him that night. You want to unread every message he sent you back. You just want to erase that part from your memory. You turn sides on the bed. Your heart impounds in your chest. It keeps thudding. You want to sleep but your thoughts wander and doesn't let you close your eyes. Maybe it was your mistake. Getting attached very easily to the people is one of your traits and you can't let people go easily. You don't beg. You just stay there floating because one day you know it won't hurt that much. Few days later resuming the old patterns of life doesn't exhaust you anymore. It doesn't take enormous efforts to get out of your bed. To cook meals, to pray, to do chores. You do everything but you know that void still remains. Then comes a day where you no longer bewail for your loss. Not relentlessly. You don't remember much of the texts you sent one another. You don't remember how he called you a cutie. There comes a day when the details of his face starts to slip from your memory. Hearing his name don't make you smile that big anymore. You still smile though but it doesn't cut you adrift. Your passion for him begins to cool down. It was gradual. Somehow he doesn't cross your mind that often. The fever was passing, slowly. It was not something, a kind of sickness. It was a real thing. May be everyone passes through that crazy period. As long as it lasts you couldn't think straight. The void in your heart is still there but it doesn't crave to be filled anymore. Why do we fall out of love ? Love is a very strong emotion. Let alone love, if it was something genuine even a bit, let's just admit that it stays with you. It stays there, right in the soft corner of your heart. You still have something. Maybe you don't but you still care. You smile when you see him happy. He crosses your mind everytime you raise your hands to pray. You feel good seeing him grow. I guess you never fall out of love, you just learn to stay away from it. You just learn to care, without showing. You just learn to pray, without him knowing. I don't know how it ends. But I have a feeling that some hearts are just meant to house voids.Not love. P.S - This is fictional Rabiya

Name: Rabiya
Question: What is love?
Answer: Yesterday I took my mom to hospital. She is been not keeping well these days. Not the covid thing. The hospital is a bit from my place and finding an auto or uber while coming back is a task. So, we went with our own vehicle. Doctor checked her and prescribed some tests. The laboratory was some 1KM away from the hospital. We went there too. I parked my scooty in the basement of the building and got done with the tests. I brought the scooty from the basement and felt that something is wrong with it. Maybe it's nothing. May be due to inclination of basement parking, I might be feeling it. I told my mom to sit and as I started driving, scooty tilted left and right. There, it was a puncture. I parked my scooty on the service road and dropped my mom to the hospital in the auto. I told her to wait there because getting a puncture repaired in an unknown place is a task. I will have to figure out the shop nearby and stuff. I came back on the same street where I parked my scooty and searched for a puncture repair shop. I took me ten minutes to get it there. It was a shabby looking little shop. Tiny. I asked the guy to check. He checked it and told me that the tube of the tire is holed and it needs to be replaced. He didn't had one. So he went to purchase. Now it was already around 30minutes since I left my mom at the hospital. The sky was getting darker and so was my mom getting tensed about me. Finally after 70–80 minutes that guy handed me my scooty and I drove back to the hospital. As expected there was my mom, sorrounded by 2–3 nurses, standing outside, crying and sobbing. As soon as she saw me, she came running to me. First I started laughing telling my mom that what's there to cry in it. Honestly, I also became a bit emotional and my eyes got filled with tears. Nurses started telling me - ‘Where were you ? Your mom is crying since an hour.’ I thanked the nurses and left. While driving I asked my mom - Why she started crying in the first place ? She started telling me - I saw in crime patrol one day. Just like you, one girl goes to repair the puncture and then she gets gang raped. You know how much I was worried. I prayed to God that - If you wish please take me but give me back my Rabiya. It left me speechless. What can I even say beyond that. As soon as we got back home, I hugged my mom tight and assured her that I am strong and I would never let anyone do that to me. Though she was barely convinced. What is love ? I don't know, actually. If this is not what love is, I don't know what it is. How intense is the war of feelings that do not fit the boundaries of words. Rabiya

Question: Do you ever feel your college life is way more toxic than you can bear? How do you cope up in such a situation?
Answer: ‘You toppers are bunch of morons. You all mug things up like parrot and vomit on answer sheet. That's what you do. We can't do that. That's why we get less marks. We can't cram things like you do.’ This what I have heard everyday, coming outside from exam hall after giving exams. Why ? Because I use lot of extra sheets in exam and sometimes I get emotional and in flow flow I tend to write alot. But that's not we are talking about it, right here. Listening to this everyday during semester exams for two years, it started hitting me from inside. I started taking less extra sheets. Why ? So that I don't get to hear people outside examhall, which eventually made me loose my marks. One day I was talking to my classmate and she was asking me about why my marks have decreased considerably. I told her the thing and she was like - ‘Seriously, Rabiya. Just because they make fun of you, you stop taking extra sheets. Stop doing this'. Everytime professor ask questions in class, I always try to give my input, even if I am not sure. This is too my classmates took seriously and they would be like - ‘Why you always raise your hand, Rabiya? Because of you we have to hear taunts of professors. Can't you just keep quiet and keep your knowledge to yourself. It's better for the whole class'. Initially, I would take this. But one day I was like fcuk it. I will be what I want to be. I will take as many extra sheets I want. I will answer every freaking question that professor asks even if I don't know the exact answer, atleast I will try. One thing you need to realize is that don't be unfair to your future self just because of other people. Once you stop reacting, people stop telling. Don't let someone dim your light just because it's shining in their eyes. Rabiya

Question: What is the most under-rated pleasure?
Answer: My friends or if I put it the other way-My non-muslim friends gifted me this Hijab (head-scarf) on my birthday.They gave me bunch of other things and it was one of them. When I opened the gift, I saw this head-scarf and it made me ‘awww'. I mean how sweet of them. Yesterday, I was driving back home and when I come back from long routes, that's when my philosophical mind gets on and I start thinking about bunch of things. So, as I was driving, this head-scarf crossed my mind, I don't know why, how but it did. Initially when I joined university, most of the people would question me about the head-scarf that I wore everytime. Some did it out of curiosity and some did it by the way of looking down upon me. The group I was previously with during my first year, they made fun of me and would ask me to remove my hijab, etc. Second year started and a student version of Indian Parliament was organized and that's when I started vibing with my then classmates and now best friends. They infact take care of hijab when it tends to slip or anything of that sort. Once I went to friends place and we all three were alone, so I removed my head-scarf and clicked few pictures. After a while one of my friend said - ‘Look at this picture, we are looking so cute in it. I mean I never asked them to do some stuff but they did it anyway. I really feel grateful to have them as my friend. Isn't it a pleasure to find people who respect your choices and decisions ? That's us on group day, they came up with the idea and we all wore hijab !!! P.S - Don't come in the comment section telling me that hijab is oppression or whatever. I have had enough of it. Let's just learn to respect other people's choices and decisions.

Question: Have you ever experienced a random act of kindness towards you from a stranger?
Answer: “No dad, I want it. Please this one is last. I promise” I said it loud standing outside a toy shop like any other stubborn kid would do. Back in 2011 - I and my family, we were roaming onto the streets of a ‘Jeddah' - a city in saudi arabia. I was 11 years old back then and I saw a huge toy shop nearby. Knowing no limits to my excitement, I ran into that shop and picked up 2 kitchen sets and 2–3 other toys. My dad was just looking at me while I was selecting all the toys. He was standing there and walking around with me. When I was done, looking at all the toys, I ran to the billing counter. Just the uncle was about to bill the items, I picked up, dad interrupted in between and asked me to pick up just one out of the two kitchen sets I chose. Both the kitchen sets were too cute and I didn't want to give up on any of it. My dad using his all time tactic told - ‘Rabiya, either select any one of the kitchen set or else I am not getting you anything’. Saying this to me, dad went and stood at the exit of the store. “No dad, I want it. Please this one is last. I promise” I said it loud standing outside a toy shop like any other stubborn kid would do. I thought time to use - crying technique, XD. I am stubborn and so is my dad. Sigh. I started crying and was requesting my dad to get me all the toys. ‘Tell me, which toy you want to buy' - I heard a uncle saying. ‘I will get it for you' he added. ‘Uncle, see my dad is asking me to choose between these two kitchen sets but I want both’, I said while making a cute crying face. ‘Okay, so the other kitchen set is on me. Come show, which one you want' said the stranger uncle. ‘No,no. Thank you. The thing is she already has too many kitchen sets at home and that's the reason I am reluctant to buy her two of it but anyway she is so stubborn, I will get her both of it. You please don't worry' - said my Dad while stopping that uncle. ‘ No brother, you know I am from Pakistan. I have a daughter. She is almost similar to your daughter. I am missing her so much today. Please let me buy your daughter this toy, it will make me happy’ - said that stranger uncle. So, he bought me that kitchen set and my dad bought me other toys. He was so generous, he just saw me crying from distance and gave me that toy as a gift. That was so kind of him. I still have that kitchen set. I don't play with it anymore. My niece and nephew, they play with it now. I clearly remember every detail about this incident. While writing this, I lived that moment again. Ahh.. a trip down to the memory lane. Some people they leave a significant imprint on your life no matter how small. Rabiya

Question: What are some of the best Bollywood dialogues we failed to notice?
Answer: There is a scene in Dear Zindagi, when Kaira (Alia Bhatt) asks Dr.Jahangir (Shahrukh Khan) - ‘You know my issues with my parents may get sorted but men, I don't know when that will happen. I am not gonna find anyone. Tell me something - Is there anything such as perfect relationship,like just one special soulmate ?’ That's when Dr. Jahangir starts explaining to Kaira - “I don't know. Kaira, I think…why just that one special soulmate ? I think one can have many soulmates in life. Different soulmates for different experiences. Like…a special music relation with someone, who share our interest in music. Or let's-get-coffee-together soulmates, perfect to have coffee with but not anything else. Or special gossip soulmate with whom you can have the perfect gossip. Or the special intellectual soulmates for all those perfect bookish discussions. So may different special soulmates. So many kinds… The romantic soulmate is just one of many. Why put the burden on one person to fulfill all your emotional needs ? It's a bit unfair.” This lines hit me hard. Like, how we start expecting everything from that one person either consciously or subconsciously ? We start romanticizing every feeling, every emotion, without even realizing it. That's how we have altogether romanticized the concept of romantic soulmate. Like it's always in our head, we expect that one single person to be there in every aspect of emotions. Isn't it true, that we have overburdened this soulmate thing. Why it always have to be your partner in every case ? Ofcourse not everyone can be our soulmate but confining it to only person is a bit unfair. Rabiya

Question: How do you feel being loved?
Answer: I am still a stranger to love. The feeling of being loved by someone is unknown to me. Love has always been a very extreme kind of feeling for me. All my life I have always feared falling in love. I have been approached by people, you know how it happens in school and college. I have always preferred to be single rather than being with someone. I have been very insecure about myself, my body, my looks, my voice and to be honest I am still insecure about it. I used to dispise the person I looked in the mirror. I have come a long way in accepting myself the way I am. I have worked alot to make myself better and today I am almost satisfied the way I look. The insecurity never let me fall in love and I never allowed anyone to come close to me. Last night I went to a wedding. It was a love-arrange marriage. The way they were looking at each other, hand holding and the happiness they had on their face really touched me. A part of me somewhere craves for a intimate-romantic relationship and whenever I see lovey-dovey couples, I kind of get a very strange feeling. Something starts running inside my blood. A feeling of not belonging to anyone, a lingering loneliness and that unexplored part of love, it gives me a very mixed feelings. As much as I want love-arrange marriage for myself, I always wonder if I would be ever able to find someone for whom I can be crazy. When it comes to me, I am very close knit person and not lot of people have access to me. I have this guard around me and I let it down only for few people. I am very emotional, when it comes to people and letting someone go aches my heart. It feels miserable when you adore and love someone and they don't feel the same for you and the sad part is you can't do anything about it. Many will not agree to me but I think - Your life actually begins after you find your person. A person you can experience your highs and lows with. Loving someone is so sacred and meaningful to me and I don't want any trial and error in this. Kehte hai opposite attracts, Jhooth hai. Hum har jagah bas apne aap ko dhundte hai aur agar woh mil jaaye toh usse sambhal rakh lena chahte hai. (They say, opposites attract. It's a lie. We only try to find ourself in another person and if we find it, we just want to keep them.) I personally feel this. You may not find the exact match of your own, but we always fall for a person who has a same basic understanding of people and life and it's subsets. How can you be with a person who completely perceive the world in a very different way as you do ? Rabiya

Question: What’s the best way to get over someone you love?
Answer: You can't keep choosing someone who doesn't choose you. You can't. Your person should be your person forever and not only when things are perfect but also when things get messy, days are less shiny and when you are hard to deal with. Just make sure that you have someone who wants to be by your side, who wants to support you and encourage you. Someone who reciprocate on the same level as you do. Someone who wants you to be happy, be fine, wants to be with you and laughs with you on lame jokes. You need this person to be your forever because there are difficult things in life and it makes you feel heavy from inside and love should not be one of those things. Love should hold your hand in those times and move forward with you. Love should be your biggest adventure and safest home. So, please don't give your best parts to someone who doesn't see value in the things you are giving to them. Be with that person - when he looks at you and without a doubt he is clear that he wants to be with you without any hesitation. Truth is just an acceptance away. Accept and move on. Rabiya

Question: How can I be happy being single?
Answer: The thing about being single is you should cherish it. Because, in a week or a lifetime, of being alone, you may only get one moment. One moment when you are not tied up in any relationship with anyone. A parent, a pet, a sibling, a friend, a partner. One moment when you stand on your own. Really truly single. And then it's gone. ~Dakota Johnson. Have you ever felt that life is better when someone is around madly in love with you ? Or to the contrary have you ever felt that life is better when you don't have anyone to look forward to ? No expectations, no disappointments. Life seems easy this way. I feel there is so much to do in life then to find someone who wants you as much as you want them or being sad over someone who doesn't. Everything takes place when it's meant to be. You need to first fill yourself with love and not anyone else. Become a whole human on your own. Fall in love with everything around you. Sunrise, little flowers blooming in the park, wander around in the city at night, go to a cafe all alone, leave some funny or meaningful notes in library books (I do this always…haha), dress up for yourself, look at the person in the mirror and ponder onto that beauty. You are absolutely gorgeous and that's the least interesting thing about you ;) Live for yourself, for your dreams and be happy on your own. Being single isn't less beautiful than being in a relationship. I promise! Rabiya

Question: When did you realize small things matter?
Answer: My school friend recently got engaged. On a lazy afternoon, out of the blue, I recieved a call from an unknown number. People generally don't call me coz I rarely pick up calls. I was free at that moment and went up on taking the call. I heard a sweet and a bit gushy voice - ‘Hey, Is this Rabiya ?’ I replied in affirmative. ‘Rabiya, it's me Sak. Remember ? Omg, I somehow found your contact number. I am so excited.’ So, a little back story. When I was in 6th standard, a new girl took admission in our class. She hailed from nearby village and would come and fro everyday around 60km. She was a bit weird. Her uniform was always dirty, her hairs were always out of the way may be because she traveled through bus, she was bit weird, one can easily spot her indifferent from the other.s She had weird eating habits, she used to be hungry even after having her tiffin. Due to her unusual behavior, no one in the class used to like her. Basically she was boycotted. I too joined the bandwagon and did what others were doing. I always knew that isn't right. If she is behaving differently, there must be reason to it. How come someone would do that to herself ? I decided to be friends with her. She told me that she doesn't live with her parents and her aunt does not treat her well, she has only one uniform and it gets washed once in a week only. Her aunt gives her too little food. Her parents have done so many efforts for sending her in our school and that's why she doesn't complain. After knowing all of this, I gained a lot of respect for her. I started bringing food for her, we became friends and were together till 10th standard. We were not best-best friends but were good friends. Everyone moved out of the city and eventually friends became strangers. It's been 6 years, I have left my hometown and haven't met my school friends even once. Receiving call from her made me so nostalgic. While talking she told me - “You know, my mom still remembers you by your name. She specifically told that please invite Rabiya first. You have been there for me always. A Thank you is a very small word…” When did I realize small things matter ? This phone call showed me two perspectives. Firstly, sometimes small things can make a big difference in other people's life. Like, I just tried knowing her, I showed her part to the rest of the class after taking her permission and things got better for her. I still think, what if I didn't made an effort in knowing her ? What if she would have remained that way till the end of school ? What if this weird behavior would have made her a negative person ? I still think about those kids who gets bullied. The way that girl was boycotted in my class, I would never forget it. No one is even ready to look at you. Everyone behaves as if you don't even exist. Secondly, I thought like it's so amazing, imagine someone out of the blue, thinks of your face, your smiles, your talk, your compliments and they get filled with so much of warmth and thankful attitude towards you. They remember you by your name, your favorite food you bought in the tiffin, how you dressed, the way you talked, they remember so much about you even if you haven't met in years. This is so satisfying. You think you are forgotten but you aren't. Rabiya

Question: Are you afraid of being alone?

I desperately need someone to love me, to talk to me, to care for me and endlessly look towards me with all the hope and love in his eyes. I many a times think that being single outweighs being in a relationship. I feel life is easier that way. No expectations, no disappointments and most importantly no heartbreaks. No matter how much I enjoy being single, often I linger on to the thought of being with someone. I crave for someone who would be there holding my hand no matter what. Sometimes silence at the night haunts me. That empty place besides me on the bed makes me feel uneasy. I wish if I had someone who would ask me about my day, it would be nice to have someone who would care for me, to be with that one crazy person sharing every bit of mine with him. Every night I go for a walk and often feel to hold on to someone's hand, to walk with him, listening to favorite songs. There are days when I just enjoy the way I am now. The feeling of not being with anyone makes me feel light and cherish my own company. There are days when I want to remain closed in my room, no interaction with anyone, just me. When I just don't want my existence to be felt on this earth. Somedays a book with a cup of tea, sitting by my window is what all I need. Honestly, I am not afraid of being alone, I am afraid of getting lost in the crowd. I am afraid of being around lot of people still feeling lonely. I am not afraid of being with someone, I am afraid of being with the wrong one. Rabiya 💫

Question: What is the most embarrassing moment that ever happened to you?
Answer: It was Republic Day 2014. I and my one friend we both were the anchors for the day. The program was supposed to begin at 9AM in the morning. By 8:45 AM, the assembly ground was full of students. Everyone gathered for the flag hoisting. Teachers, sisters, brothers and fathers everyone was present on the ground. Now, the chief guest for the day showed up pretty late and we were eagerly waiting for him to come, so that we get to eat the cake and chips after the flag hoisting. Finally, around 9:40 AM, his car made an entry through the gate and stopped near the main building of school. Few teachers were already present there to recieve him. We all got pretty excited and thought that he would walk towards the stage and after the welcome ceremony the flag hoisting would take place. But it didn't happen that way. He was clearly visible from the stage, he showed his tiny little finger to one of the teacher and asked for going to washroom. Every student was laughing silently after seeing this XD. I slowly whispered into the ear of my friend - “Yeh kaise cheif guest hai ? Late aaye hai, upar se ghar se halka hokar bhi nai aaye" (“What type of cheif guest he is ? He is late already and have not done his business from home”) Now, I heard the same thing coming out of those huge speakers installed in the school premises and I also heard students laughing. Tubelight me, realized that I forgot to turn my mic off. I could see my class teacher looking at me with his haunted eyes. I was like - please sorry. Meanwhile the father, who was principle of our school was from south and his hindi was very weak. He said to me, Rabiya, don't you know speaking in English is compulsory in school campus. What did you just say ? Why everyone is laughing ? Will you please repeat in English ? I was like - “No father, nothing important. Just slip of tongue. I am sorry”. Everyone teased me for this incident for few weeks even small kids from primary section. It was hell embarrassing and I walked hiding myself from every teacher for a week. Thank you for reading :) Image source - Google. Rabiya 💫

Question: Is there's any decision that your parents took for you but ultimately it proved to be a wrong decision?
Answer: It all started when one day I came back crying from my coaching classes. I was in 11th standard and my classes for pre medical entrance exams used to end by 7–8 in the evening. That day my scooty was punctured, so I went by auto. I was returning back home from the coaching, I was feeling frightened to sit in an auto alone, so I decided to walk back home. The distance was around 3 kilometers. As soon as I walked few paces, 3–4 guyz were standing at the cross road and they started some shitty things. This was the first time, I was experiencing eve-teasing, that too in the middle of a busy road. I ignored and started walking faster and faster. I walked for another 5–7 mins, I don't know but I got this gut feeling that someone is following me. I looked back again and again. A man in his 30's was moving his bike slowly and slowly little away from and everytime I looked back to check he awkwardly smiled at me. I was not understanding anything, what was going on? I walked and walked then finally after 2–3 mins, a lady was waiting for an auto. I went and stood next to her and started talking with her. Thankfully, she was going to the same area as mine. An auto came and I came back home. I was very disturbed by this incident, I didn't tell my parents anything about this. I just informed my mom that I won't be going to coaching for few days as there are no important topics to be taught. 1 week passed, my parents asked me about my coaching and I again denied going for it. They somehow felt that something is wrong. After they tried so many times, I told them the incident and they were mad at me for not telling them this earlier. They told me that this incident should not bother me. I need to be strong. I am a brave girl, etc,etc. Now next day, my dad bought me a mobile phone. A personal, my very own mobile phone. My parents are very strict and getting a phone that too personal, was not into my wildest of dreams as well. I was on cloud 9. My happiness knew no boundaries. It alll started from here. One thing I didn't get was that how and why a mobile phone solved my problem? But anyway who cares? I got my phone. Now, next day I went to school just for flaunting my new phone. The posters in bold letters hung outside every classroom stating - “mobile phones are strictly prohibited” did not exist for me after that day. It was 2016, few people in class had the phone and few didn't. I started showing my phone to every girl sitting around me, show off you know. Now, I was sitting on the fifth or sixth bench and when my phone took the stroll of an entire row is out of my knowledge. All of a sudden, I heard my not so favorite physics sir screaming in loud voice - “Whose phone is this ?”. I didn't seem to care because I thought my phone must be somewhere here around the girls near me. He then raised his hands and showed the phone and asked again. I stared at him in shock and stood up slowly. Then you know the drill, he took me to principal office. Now, the principal wanted to call my parents. I told him that they are out of town, which was a lie, obviously. He then asked for my father's phone number. Now, I thought of an idea, I gave him my dad's old phone number which was out of service. He tried calling on that number but all in vain, all thanks to me. Then, I recieved a suspension letter for a week. Anyway I hated going to school. My parenst came to know about this incident after 2 days and since then they regret getting me a mobile phone till now and I think they will continue to do so until I get married..lol. Meanwhile my parents after knowing that reason for my suspension was the very mobile phone they got me, Thank you for reading. Rabiya 💫

Question: Share something you're grateful for today?
Answer: My nani (grandmother) is diabetic. A week ago she did her quarterly medical check up. Reports stated that she has increased level of blood sugar and doctor advised her to take insulin injections. Injecting insulin is an easy task and I know how to do it. Now, my nani became a bit nervous as to who will inject her insulin everyday, then I assured her that I will do that. We live in the same apartment just the different buildings. So, everynight when I go for a walk around 10PM, I first give her injection and then proceed with my walking. I am always in hurry, I hastly open the door with keys, wash my hand, take out the injection and give it to her and leave. My nani resides at 9th floor and when I wait outside for the elevator she stands at the doorway until I go. She is so cute. She recites some quranic verses for me and gives me loads of blessings. Such a small act of mine, infront of her is much valuable. Whenever I cook something special, or when I bring her medicines, take her to hospital, bring her stuff from DMart, she always gives me lot of blessings and prayers. Actually my uncle (mama) lives abroad, so my nani and my aunty live alone. So, we make sure to get them the needful. While I was walking yesterday, it put in gush of emotional gratitude. Like I have so many people in my life who appreciate such a small acts of mine and give me lot of blessings in return. My nani calls my mom everyday (mother-daughter talks you know), when my mom isn't available, I pick up the call, tell her that mom isn't at home and will call her later and I hang up without listening the other side. How mean? Can't I talk to her for a minute or two ? Can't I ask her about her well being ? It reminds of good old days, when I used to live at Nashik and came for vacation here at Nani' place. That happiness, that peace is lost nowadays. I used to stay at nani' place for whole of the vacation and still would crave for more. Now, my nani just stays in nearby building but I don't even visit her unless due to some work. Isn't it ironic that we ignore the ones who love us and love the ones who ignore us? We the so called 'digital generation' do lot of stuff to seek attention of strangers on the internet. We seek validation and recognition from random people on web but fail to appreciate the presence of people around us who willingly accepts us the way we are. Strange, isn't it? I was pondering on these things so much while walking and it instantly reminded me of an answer I wrote about toxic parenting. So many people reached through comments and messages stating that they have narcissistic parents and family. They feel depressed and don't have anyone to reach out to. I can't even imagine the situation of these kids who have to go through this. Parents and family are suppose to be a safe place for kids. Home and parents are meant to be paradise for kids. They are the first people we reach out to when in trouble but what about these kids who don't even have a safe and happy place to grow? I lost my grand pa in this pandemic and he was the coolest grandpa ever. I have spent so much time with him in my early childhood and then so called grew up and lost my connect with him. After he was gone, I realized how beautiful the bond I shared with him was ? I wish I could have spend more time with him. It's really true that we only appreciate people and things when there are no more with us. This is what my nani gave me for Eidi. These envelopes were made by my cousin on the instruction of nani ji. She is cute, isn't it? The envelope reads - To Rabiya, May you become a successful lawyer. May god bless you with a good spouse. Stay happy and blessed always. Also get married soon :) I think this is gift plus bribe plus blackmail all rolled into one ;) I spent the money present inside but I still have the envelope with me. It's so precious. Thank you for reading. Rabiya 💫

Question: When someone is single, is the person lonely, or is that freedom? Why?

Question: What is the most difficult thing in the world?
Answer: Right now, I am sitting outside the emergency ward of a hospital in my city. There is so much going around me. A 14–15 years old girl is sitting and crying on the shoulders of her dad. Her mother has suffered a brain stroke and is in ICU since a month now. There are lot of people around me. Doctors and nurses are making there way in and out of the emergency ward. An ambulance arrived few minutes ago, the ward boys quickly bought the stretcher inside with a man on it. The family of that man, I don't know but they must be present somewhere here only, waiting for a hope. Everyone here has kind of same feeling here. There is an awkward silence. People are sitting here with just one thing that is hope. The hope that they will get to see their loved ones again, they will not have to take their dead body at home, that some miracle could save their loved one. When one person of your family is ill and is hospitalized, everyone at home has some kind of uncomforting feeling. Everytime there is a phone call from hospital, there is a fear inside. This feeling doesn't go away unless the patient gets back home. The people who are around me, I have never met them in my life and will never see them again but somehow I can feel them. I know what mental state they must be in right now. Every second feels like an hour, that hopeless expressions of the doctor, when you hear - we can't guarantee anything, it feels like end of the world. Those words rip you apart. People die here at hospital everyday, the pain that every family goes through after loosing someone close is unbearable. Many people say that the show must go on, life goes on with or without people. But it is not easy to implement such things in life. It's not very easy to move on in life. You wake up to a family member everyday, you see them as a very first face in the morning, you share smiles, secrets, happiness, pain, sorrow and everything. One day they are no more a part of your life. You can't see them anymore, you can't feel them anymore. It takes years to ease the pain of loss but memories remain with you forever and deep down you miss them every single day, their absence haunts you like anything. My aunt has some neurological condition and she has to get admitted for 2 days every six months to get her treatment done. She is all good and fine. Uncle is out of town, so I insisted to stay with her. Courts and hospitals are the two places where we get to feel almost every type of emotion. Some are happy, some are sad, some have got hope, some are hopeless, some are just visitors and some just get to see this till the very end of their life. I remember a year back, I was doing an internship at an NGO, there I met an aunty who was HIV positive. I wanted to talk to her, but never gathered the courage to do so. I often used to smile at her and greet her good morning. She used to smile and wave at me. I must say her smile was the fakest smile I have ever come across. Living with a disease where you know it will definitely kill you one day. Where those medicines keep you somehow alive for few months. People shun you and look down towards you just because of someone else's mistake. The difficult part here is to still keep smiling. Putting that fake smile on your face when you are crying inside. Staying silent with some sort of despair and hope when you are screaming inside. Pretending that you are okay, when you are in extreme pain. Facing the reality when you just want to escape it. The night is dark and long, but sooner or later, sun will eventually rise. It's beautiful isn't it ? How it hurts but we still don't give up. ~ 25th May 2021 Rabiya 💫

Question: What were some of the unforgettable incidents from your school life?
Answer: It was 3rd of August 2012, just a day before my birthday. I was very excited, as soon as I came back from school, hastily had lunch, took some money from my dad and ran towards a shop to buy chocolates for my birthday. In my head, right now I am standing on that shop. The conversation with the shopkeeper went like this - He - Beta, you study at Saint Chavara, right ? I - Yes uncle. He - Do you know Prajakta ? I - Yes, she is my senior at school. But why are you asking me this ? He - She is no more. She met with an accident while returning from school. The rickshaw driver is also dead. I - No I don't know who is Prajakta ? And I don't study in Saint Chavara. I couldn't believe what my ears heard. I don't know what happened to me at that moment ? Prajakta, she was the only sister of my classmate, Kartik. She often used to visit our class. She was the head girl of the school. I saw her in the morning assembly only. How can she die ? Kartik, what happened to him ? How will he react ? Her beautiful face (and when I say beautiful she was damn beautiful), her loving nature, the way she used to arrange kids for assembly, her voice while singing the chorus, everything was revolving around me while I was returning home. After I reached home, I started crying. I don't know why ? She was just a senior. Just interacted with her few times. Just saw her from distant always. Never shared a bond with her. But I could feel her absence. When we are around few people, even though we don't interact with each other, they subconsciously become a part of our life. We may not see them everyday, we may not even know them properly but somewhere we get habitual to their presence. At night I received a call from a classmate. She told me that - Kartik needs to be operated coz he is injured so bad, their school auto was hit by a huge truck and he, his sister and driver, this 3 people were only present in the auto at the time of the accident. Kartik somehow survived the hit but the other two died on the spot. My classmate also told me that on that particular day, Prajakta asked her parents to let her and Kartik go by scooty to school, but parents denied. Now, the only regret their parents has is - they wish they would have allowed her to go by scooty that day. May be she would have been said. But it is said that no one escape death. While I am writing this I still can't believe that Prajakta is no more. Her beautiful face is infront of my eyes right now. How life is uncertain, you know ? Whenever I remember this incident, I think she must have also planned for her future. What about her dreams, the things she wanted to do, the places she wanted to visit, her ambitions, everything died with her. A huge filter was donated by her parents to the school which read as - In The Loving Memory Of Prajakta. Whenever Kartik drops message in the school group, it always reminds me of Prajakta. I was never close to her, but still I remember her very often. I wonder how her family must be coping up with their loss. We come across lot of people in our lives but few people become a strong part of our memory. Rabiya 💫

Question: What is a split-second decision you made that changed your life?
Answer: I was standing inside the airport. Tickets, boarding pass everything was ready. Four and a half years of student visa, my college, my hostel, my companions everything was decided. I somehow agreed to go to Russia for becoming a doctor. My father always wanted me to be a Gynecologist. When I appeared for medical entrance for the first time, I didn't score too good. I told my dad that, “See it's not happening. I have somehow failed to meet your expectations. I want to call it a quit. I have a backup ready, can I do that ?” To which my dad replied- “I don't want to pressurize you in any form. People fail in entrance exams, it's alright. There is nothing to be ashamed about it. If you wish you can take a drop, I have seen your hardwork, so why not give another chance to yourself ? I decided to take a drop and appeared for medical entrance again. I somehow managed to fetch a seat in government medical college but not in MBBS. Another disappointment….ughh. My dad told me to go to Russia. He never forced to do anything. He just wanted me to try. I thought for a while, I told my dad few things and denied going abroad for further studies. I thought I didn't deserve it. I again thought for few days. When I was in school, I was never allowed to go to picnic, no parties, no night-outs, no hanging out with friends. I always somehow felt caged. I always wanted to fly freely. I thought that the freedom which I always longed for is infront of me. I will go abroad, there will be no one who will restrict me, I will have a complete authority on myself. This idea of freedom fantasized me. I agreed going to Russia. Desperation and hunger can make you do anything. That was so selfish of me. Visa was granted, I was admitted in a college, my hostel was decided, it was whole solid proof plan. I was getting everything which I wanted, but I was not happy from inside. I was feeling guilty. Something wasn't letting me sleep at night. Why was I not happy ? This is what I always wanted. Freedom, no restrictions, no limitations. But something was eating me inside. The day of departure arrived. I and my dad left for Mumbai. Whole of the while, I was thinking about my decision. I felt something was awfully wrong with me. I bid my Dad, a final goodbye and entered the airport. The boarding pass was stamped, my flight was ready to fly. I asked myself - Listen, how can you be so shallow ? You are putting your parents on stake. Just talk to mom and dad, this is what you will have to do..I know they will understand. I was standing on the air-bridge, just 15 mins before the take-off. I called my dad - Dad, I am really sorry. I don't want to go..please. He told me to come back outside the airport. I had a talk with my parents and they did understand me. One thing I learned from this - Once a NO, doesn't mean it always will be a NO. Now, I can hangout with my friends, I can attend parties, but I don't go now also. Earlier I thought I don't go because I wasn't allowed and now I don't go by a choice. Sometimes we feel that limitations and restrictions which are imposed upon us is unfair. It is unfair sometimes. But most of the time, there is a reason behind it. I think whatever things I was subject to, it has shaped me for how I am right now. Howsoever, I am right now, I would have never been better than this. I so much happy and content with myself. Just because you don't get to attend a birthday party that doesn't mean it's the end of the world. That birthday parties you don't attend, the nights you don't hangout and stay and work on yourself, will reap you benefits in future. You are just a decision away from an entire different life. Image - Google. Rabiya 💫

Question: What is something everyone should know?
Answer: At whatever stage of life you are at right now, don't just let it go. Don't treat it like a fleeting phase. Or if you are in college don't waste it wishing to be already graduated and having a job and making money. If you are single don't waste it wishing to be in love with someone. If you are old don't waste it wishing to be dead already 😜 Everything you wish for will come in due time. Things will reach out to you when they are good for you. Just wait and let things happen. There is no point in wishing about something which you will eventually get in future. There is nothing like looking back and feeling sad about those years because you were missing out on something which you already had in pursuit of hoping for something better. Ofcourse it's important to make goals and reach them at earliest, but in the process don't neglect the present because this things you have right now you won't get it again. We often ponder upon things and wish that a certain thing should happen to us right now, everything will come to you when you are ready for it. Eventually every part of your puzzle will fall in place to create a wonderful masterpiece. Just embrace the place you are at right now, it's lovely to be here and journey ahead is beautiful as well but just don't miss on stars while waiting for the moon ✨. Rabiya 💫

Question: How can I force myself to study?
Answer: Open your phone and start scrolling. Seriously, if you need to force yourself to study then please don't do it. How long will you force yourself to study ? For 2–4 hours, okay ? Then what after that man ? Do you need to force yourself to use phone ? Do you need to force yourself to play games ? Do you need to force yourself for wasting time ? Most probably no, right ? Your dreams, your goals, your targets should scare the hell out of you, It should scare you so much that you no longer press that snooze button, You no longer need to ask yourself that - Am I in a mood to study today ? You no longer get distracted by the internet world. Your dreams should hit you like a train, once you miss these train, it's never coming back. You know, I have appeared for examinations with only 45 minutes of sleep. My eyes used to get shut while reading, I have drank black coffee whole of the nights, my parents used to scold me for not sleeping, but did that stop me ? No, because it's Now or Never. Just start. Question: What is the best piece of advice you could give someone about life?
Answer: Last week, I was having lunch with my friends at a restaurant after we were done with our university work. We were simply cracking jokes and laughing that's when I realized something. I stopped laughing and I was just looking at my own reflection that I could see in the glass which was infront of me. I realized that - Life is nothing but moments. That jokes we cracked and laughed about were moments. Moments come and go. Life is all about moments. That fight you had with your best-friend, that whole night you stayed up for a project, that frightening moments before a interview, everything is just matter of few moments. Those days you spend talking to a guy you thought you would end up together was just a moment. That exam you failed, that race you never won, that presentation you messed up, that game you lost is a moment. Those nights when you cried to sleep, that phases of loneliness, that day when you were just crying aloud sitting on the floor, everything is moment. Every high and every low, every up and every down and everything in between is moments. You may remember these moments or you may even forget them. But you know what ? You will always remember the people you spent your moments with and the way you felt. The way she made you smile, the way she was a light in the darkness of your boring life, the way she was a cool breeze of air, that patch of happiness she was, the way she cared for you, the way she gave you all of her attention, the way she made you feel special, everything was a moment and it passed. All of these moments, people and the way they make us feel makes bigger moments called Life. All in all, life is the collection and combination of these moments. So, appreciate the moments you are given, and people with whom you share those moments, because no matter how happy or tragic a moment is eventually it will end. So, Hug a little tighter, Smile a little more curvier, Cry a little louder, Smile a little harder, Forgive a little quicker, Care a little more, Love a hell lot more deeper. Because these are the moments you will remember one day, when you will be sitting on your arm chair and will be counting days, these moments will come across as a flashback infront of your eyes, and only thing you would regret - I wish I could just go back and live a little more. Question: What do you do to motivate yourself when you are about to give up?
Answer: Let me tell you a incident which happened today morning. I kept water in a container on a gas stove to boil for my green tea (not a health freak, okay) After few minutes the water started to simmer and was on the verge of boiling. Accidentally I turned off the main supply of the gas stove and the water which was about to boil, settled down. I turned on the main supply again, and water boiled and I had my green tea. Now, let me tell you I am a keen observer and also an overthinker. So here you go. After the above scenario, I started to think - How the water that was about to boil, settled down just because supply was cut for few seconds ? What if water had a capacity to boil itself (please bear with me) ? and many such similar questions. After few hours I realized the rocket science 😂. Water for boiling was dependent on a external source, and as soon as the source was cut, even for a few seconds, it stopped boiling. Similar is the case for motivation. You can watch hours and hours of motivational YouTube videos. Listen to the success stories of a billionaire or a struggle of a student who outperformed everyone. Motivation can be found anywhere. Motivational videos are everywhere like it's confetti. But does this motivation lasts ? It may last for few hours, or few days or even few weeks. But, what after that ? As your motivation goes down, your efforts, productivity everything declines, right ? This is inevitable. It has to happen. As long as you seek external motivation, one day or the other it will fade away. So, why not have some internal source of motivation ? Question: When did you realize that you had grown up?
Answer: Yesterday I and my mom went for COVID-19 Rapid Test. We were getting all the symptoms. We reached the hospital. I parked the car on the opposite side of road. We were just about to cross the road, I realized someone just hold my hand from behind, I looked and, That was my mom. When the nurse was about to put the Covid testing strip into the my mum' nose she looked at me and said- Rabiya, come here. Hold my hand. I am afraid. When we were waiting for the reports in the waiting area, my mum became very emotional. She was worried. I consoled - Mom, why are you crying ? Everything will be alright. Just relax. Thankfully, we both tested negative for covid and we got back home. While I went to bed last night, I realized the reversal of roles, Until yesterday, I was the one who hold the hands of my parents while crossing the road, I was the one who was afraid while getting an injection, I was the one who was consoled by my parents. But the sides have swaped now. I am no longer a kid. I am no longer that little girl, I have grown up. My upbringing is done in the most beautiful manner. I was never considered a fragile flower, rather I am that typical touch me not flower. I can drive, I can cook, I can get out of the house even in the middle of the night if it's required. My parents have made me a strong girl. My parents have always heard from the people that Ohh, you don't have a son. What will you do ? It's better to have a son. I never agreed with such thought process. I have always made sure that my parents should never feel that - they don't have a son and for that matter my parents never realized the need of a son. I was just thinking, I am 22 now. By the time I complete my graduation I will be 24. Eventually I will get married. I will have to leave my parents and go. My time with my parents is not much left. Just 2–3 years may be. Time for the good bye. This hit me like a train. I was just wondering, how my parents will be alone in their old age. I just wish I can stay with them forever. I always tell my parents that - I am never getting married, never leaving them alone. Last night I was convinced that those people were right. It's good to have a son as well. Because eventually daughters get married and they leave their parents. I was just thinking I wish I had a brother, at least he who would have stayed with my parents till the end. These many thoughts kept me awake for so long last night. I was just wondering that if I could pause this time or I could delay the ageing of my parents or if I could just change my gender. Such thoughts hit me very often and I find myself in a dilemma of situations. It's funny, how day by day nothing changes, But when we look back, everything is different. Some women feel liberated wearing the clothes of their choice, some women feel liberated wearing revealing clothes, some women feel liberated nude and likewise some women feel liberated when covered. When I criticize your nudity -I am a conservative. When you criticize my hijab -You are an intellectual. Ah…Really ? When I wear a Hijab, it makes people to look at me beyond my looks or physical appearance. It shows the real me. It often becomes a initiator of the conversation of my faith and I feel good when I talk to people what Hijab is and why I wear it. What do you think about this picture ? What comes to your mind when you see a girl or a woman in hijab ? Do you think that I am oppressed by my religion to wear a Hijab ? Do you think that ‘I am must be obedient and docile’ ? Hijab being oppression or not has become a major issue nowadays. People often associate that a hijabi women is submissive and lacks freedom. As a hijabi university student, I am often asked about the purpose of hijab. People also ask - was I forced to wear it ? What's the objective of wearing a hijab ? As a hijabi, people always have views about me. They either think of me - Little do they know that I wear Hijab because I love to wear it. Infact I am proud of myself wearing a hijab. I often get judged wearing a Hijab. People consider me as a conservative or traditional girl. They ignore me and don't even make an effort to know me. People - I am also like any other ordinary girl who got some witty sense of humour and has got some brain. I am a simple and innocent human being trying to live a beautiful and peaceful life. Hijab sets me apart from others. It acts a distinguishing factor. I wear it so that I am identified as a practicing women of Islam. I feel proud when people know that I am a muslim when I enter a room. I don't want to hide my religion or culture. I am not the one who hides it. I believe my beliefs and my faith should be accepted by others. People should respect one another, if not love, regardless of their religion, ethnicity or culture. It's more on the humanitarian ground. Am I oppressed ? No, I am not oppressed. Wearing a Hijab was my personal choice - Alone. No one forced upon me neither my parents nor the society. It was my choice. I am also the first person in my extended family who did her schooling from a English school. My elder sister is the first person in my extended family who runs an office on her own and also has a staff of 10 people working under her. As a matter of fact I don't have a brother. My father gave us all the liberty when it came to education, to pursue what interests us. My hijab doesn't stop me from doing anything I want in anyway. I don't feel oppressed wearing Hijab, but I do feel oppressed when people try to convince me to remove it. For me a real oppression is when you deny a person of a choice. So yes, forcing someone to veil or wear a hijab amounts to oppression. Similarly forcing them to take the hijab off is also an oppression. Also it's an undisputed fact that some women are forced to wear a hijab and are oppressed. Does the Hijab is only for women ? Hijab denotes a modest lifestyle. It applies for men and women both. When men wear tight T-shirts showing their muscles they also go against the modesty described in Islam. Modesty lies in the character and lifestyle of a person. Quran when stating about hijab does not adress the women first. Indeed wearing a headscarf is a form of Hijab but people don't realize that hijab is much more than that. Quran first commands men to lower their gaze and not to stare at women. Sikhs wearing turban, Christian wearing crucifix, jews wearing kippah, women from different faiths wearing ‘pallu', etc. are the similar expression of faith as a Hijab. Lastly I want to tell that Hijab is my way of expressing myself. It's my way of telling people that I want to be judged on the basis of my character, my behavior and my personality rather than being judged on my appearances. I want to be heard before being seen. Hijab is the form of liberation ; not the form of oppression. Until we meet again, Rabiya
